key_sub: A pairs with T (or U), G with C; each codon has three bases.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a double helix of two antiparallel strands, with adenine paired to thymine (two hydrogen bonds) and guanine to cytosine (three); base pairs are 0.34 nm apart. Griffith, Avery and Hershey–Chase showed DNA is the genetic material; Meselson and Stahl showed replication is semi-conservative. DNA polymerase works 5′ → 3′, making Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.

Transcription copies a gene into RNA; in eukaryotes introns are spliced out. Translation reads mRNA codons on ribosomes; the triplet code is degenerate, universal and starts at AUG. The lac operon switches genes on when lactose is present. DNA fingerprinting uses VNTRs.

Example

30% A. % G?

(100 − 60) ÷ 2

Answer: 20%

Example

Complementary to ATGC?

A–T, G–C

Answer: TACG

Common mistakes

  • Pairing A with G.
  • Counting the stop codon as an amino acid.
  • Saying the genetic code overlaps.

faq.a: Each new DNA double helix keeps one original strand and has one newly made strand.

faq.q: How does the lac operon work?
faq.a: Without lactose a repressor blocks the operator; lactose (the inducer) removes it so the genes for lactose use are transcribed.

items.q: A DNA segment has 4,790 base pairs. How many hydrogen bonds hold it together if 30% of its bases are adenine?
items.e: A = T = 30%, G = C = 20%. A–T pairs = 2,874 (2 bonds), G–C pairs = 1,916 (3 bonds): total = 11,496.

items.q: What does the Human Genome Project show about the number of human genes?
c: every base is part of a gene
items.e: Less than 2% of the genome codes for proteins.

items.q: A DNA segment has 4,570 base pairs. How many hydrogen bonds hold it together if 30% of its bases are adenine?

items.q: What is splicing?
c: removing introns and joining exons in the primary RNA transcript of eukaryotes
items.e: A cap and a poly-A tail are also added.

items.q: In the DNA of a bacterium, 23% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are guanine?
items.e: A + T = 46%, so G + C = 54%, and guanine = half of that: 27%.

In the DNA of a fish, 21% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are guanine?
items.e: A + T = 42%, so G + C = 58%, and guanine = half of that: 29%.

items.q: What does 'the code is universal' mean?
c: the same codons code for the same amino acids in nearly all organisms
codons are read in any order
items.e: This allows genetic engineering.

items.e: A + T = 34%, so G + C = 66%, and cytosine = half of that: 33%.

items.q: What is the function of tRNA?
c: it brings the correct amino acid to the ribosome by matching its anticodon to the codon
it carries the code from DNA
items.e: It has a clover-leaf shape.
